verdict.rationale: Grafana's own docs describe Grafana SLO (in Grafana Cloud) as a product feature for defining SLIs and SLOs and deciding "how to react" when service falls short, so the core SLO-definition part is directly supported. The pack never mentions error budgets or burn-rate alerting, and general Grafana Alerting evidence does not stand in for SLO burn-rate alerts. Missing for 10: explicit error-budget tracking, documented burn-rate alert rules, independent or hands-on corroboration of the SLO feature.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can define SLOs with error budgets and burn-rate alerts

citations.quote: By creating SLIs (Service Level Indicators) and SLOs, you define what an acceptable level of service is and how to react if you are not providing the expected level of service.
Grafana SLO (Service Level Objective) provides a framework for measuring the quality of service you provide to users.
With Grafana SLO, you can create metrics to measure the quality of the service you provide users.
